title: Data → Model → Prediction — The Mystery Package Line
key_insight: An ML pipeline is the same kind of route: collect data, clean it, train a model, and use that model on new inputs.
body:
## The Mystery Package Line

A parcel company keeps losing boxes between arrival and delivery. Drawing every station reveals where each box changes and where mistakes enter.

An ML pipeline is the same kind of route: collect data, clean it, train a model, and use that model on new inputs.

Keeping the route visible makes a prediction traceable. When an answer looks wrong, you can inspect one station instead of blaming the whole system.
common_mistakes: Changing serving-time cleaning without retraining the model.
Saving the model but not its learned preprocessing.
Running a pipeline without recording versions or data-quality counts.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “The Mystery Package Line” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Every ML project needs a traceable path from source data to a monitored prediction.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “The Mystery Package Line” story, explain Data → Model → Prediction without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
